chunks: 5904 - Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, who said:

A favor is only a true favor when it is with one possessing nobility or religion. Salat (prayer) is the means of nearness for every God-conscious person. Hajj is the jihad of every weak person. Everything has a zakat, and the zakat of the body is sawm (fasting). The jihad of a woman is good conduct toward her husband. Seek sustenance through charity. Whoever is certain of recompense is generous in giving. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends down assistance according to the burden. Fortify your wealth through zakat. Proper measure is half of livelihood. No person who is moderate becomes poor. Few dependents are one of the two eases. One who makes du'a (supplication) without action is like one who shoots without a bowstring. Affection is half of intellect. Anxiety is half of decrepitude. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends down patience according to the measure of the affliction. Whoever strikes his hand upon his thigh at the time of affliction, his reward is nullified. Whoever saddens his parents has been undutiful to them.

key_terms.التَّقْدِيرُ: measured moderation and sound management in livelihood
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, by which wealth is protected
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: charity, presented as a means of seeking sustenance
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), described here as a means of nearness to Allah
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: hajj (pilgrimage), described as the jihad of the weak
key_terms.الْمُصِيبَةِ: affliction or calamity, in proportion to which patience is granted
key_terms.حُسْنُ التَّبَعُّلِ: good conduct of a wife toward her husband
key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْجَسَدِ: the body's zakat, identified here as fasting

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about charity, worship, patience, and conduct with parents?
ai.summary: This hadith gathers concise ethical teachings on worship, charity, livelihood, family conduct, and patience during affliction. It presents salat (prayer), hajj, sawm (fasting), zakat, generosity, moderation, and dutifulness to parents as foundational traits of a God-conscious life.
